tooling.message:
docs(guidance): skill lernapps-commit for a linear history and structured messages

## Intent

Work in app repos reached main as merge or fast-forwarded commits with free-form messages, so the history was neither linear nor explained. Every piece of work should land as one squash commit with a message that says why it was made.

## Key changes

- A new skill lernapps-commit: bring a branch into main by squash (squash merge of the pull request, or git merge --squash), never a merge commit. Every message is a conventional commit with the sections Intent, Key changes and Dependencies and side effects, without file lists, in the language of the repo's history.
- lernapps-app tells the assistant to load the skill before every commit and every merge into main. AGENTS.md stays under its word limit.
- The first-version plan brings work into main with git merge --squash instead of --ff-only; the increment plan squash-merges its pull request.
- The package exports the new skill.
